subject: MAP alignment & contingency: AcroHealth evaluation window
messages:
From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
To: Sarah Lim <sarah.lim@acrohealth.com>
Cc: Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwood.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-10-01T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: MAP alignment & contingency: AcroHealth evaluation window

Sarah —

Following up from yesterday's call, attached is a concise mutual action plan (MAP) draft that aligns our evaluation gates with your internal acceptance milestones. Key points: 
- Evaluation window target: Nov 15 - Nov 29 (2-week eval).
- Acceptance criteria draft in tab 'Gate 2'.
- Contingency: a staggered cutover if procurement PO slips more than 10 business days.

I'm flagging two immediate asks so we can keep the go-live within the quarter: 
1) Can procurement confirm a tentative PO approval date by EOD Tuesday so we can lock capacity?
2) Can AcroHealth provide a short list of 3 critical datasets we should prioritize for the first run?

Attachments: ACRO_MAP_v2.xlsx (MAP draft), SOC2-evidence-summary.pdf (requested items list).

I'll schedule a 30-min sync with Camila and Grace to walk the contingency lanes if procurement risk is material.

Thanks,
Jordan Blake
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
jordan.blake@redwood.com | +1 415 555 0142

From: Sarah Lim <sarah.lim@acrohealth.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
Cc: AcroHealth Procurement <procurement@acrohealth.com>
Date: 2026-10-02T11:08:00-07:00
Subject: Re: MAP alignment & contingency: AcroHealth evaluation window

Hi Jordan —

Thanks for the MAP — looks good at a high level. Two points from our side that change the risk profile: 
- Procurement has flagged a potential vendor review on Oct 20 that could push our PO by ~2 weeks (they're re-evaluating a budget line).
- Our security team asked for one more artifact for SOC2 evidence: encryption-at-rest implementation detail (we can share a short note by tomorrow).

We want to keep the Nov 15 eval start if possible, but if procurement slips we will likely need the staggered cutover plan you mentioned. Procurement is looped here — procurement@acrohealth.com — and will confirm next steps.

Sarah
Sarah Lim | Head of Data & Analytics, AcroHealth
sarah.lim@acrohealth.com | 617-202-8810

From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
To: Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwood.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.com>, Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-10-02T13:30:00-07:00
Subject: Fwd: MAP alignment & contingency: AcroHealth evaluation window

Folks — forwarding Sarah's note. Procurement noise looks likely to cause a 10–14 day PO slip, which will impact our reserved capacity booking and the Nov 15 eval start. I'm proposing two operational responses: 

Option A (preferred): Keep Nov 15 start by using a scoped-in pilot (single-model, 25% traffic, synthetic dataset) so we can hit evaluation gates for product/ops sign-off while procurement finalizes the PO. Requires short-term credit approval (~2 weeks).

Option B: Re-baseline the MAP to shift evaluation start to Nov 30, keep full scope but accept the slip; escalate for a limited credit accommodation to retain the preferred GPU pool.

Immediate asks: 
- Priyom, can you approve a two-week credit exception (up to $15k) to preserve capacity if Procurement misses the Oct 20 window?
- Camila/Grace, can you review the MAP_v2.xlsx and flag which milestones must remain fixed vs. which can be decoupled?

I'll draft an exec escalation if procurement confirms a delay.

From: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>, Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwood.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-10-03T09:45:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: MAP alignment & contingency: AcroHealth evaluation window

Jordan —

I reviewed the MAP and the two options. Approving a short-term credit exception up to $15k is acceptable provided we document clear rollback criteria:
- If procurement hasn't issued PO by Oct 27, we move to Option B and stop using dedicated capacity (fall back to hosted with capacity throttles).
- Any usage beyond the $15k cap reverts to standard billing and we cut sprint scope.

Camila: mark Gate 1 (smoke tests, security checklist) as immutable. Everything in Gate 2 can be scoped down for a pilot.

Jordan — please prepare a 1-slide escalation note for execs with the cost/benefit of short-term credit vs delayed evaluation. I'll sign it off.

Priyom
Senior Sales Ops | Redwood Inference
priyom.das@redwood.com

From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
To: Sarah Lim <sarah.lim@acrohealth.com>, AcroHealth Procurement <procurement@acrohealth.com>
Cc: Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwood.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.com>, Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-10-05T16:05:00-07:00
Subject: Exec summary + updated MAP (MAP_v2) and proposed contingency decision

Sarah / Procurement —

Per our internal alignment, attaching the updated MAP (ACRO_MAP_v2.xlsx) and a 1-slide executive summary. Key decisions: 
- Redwood approved a two-week credit exception (cap $15k) to preserve Nov 15 pilot start under a scoped pilot (Option A).
- Immutable items: Gate 1 security & smoke tests.
- If PO not issued by Oct 27, both sides accept re-baselining to Nov 30 (Option B) and we transition to full-scope evaluation then.

Please confirm procurement's estimated PO date by close of business Oct 6 so we can lock GPU pools and finalize the pilot scope.

Attachments: ACRO_MAP_v2.xlsx, SOW_draft_v1.docx (for procurement review).

Thanks — Jordan
